name: Task Flow Diagram
description:
A task flow represents the sequence of actions required to complete a particular goal. It focuses on the path through a defined task and can include user actions, system responses and decision points.

Task flows help designers examine whether necessary steps are understandable, appropriately ordered and unnecessarily complex.
whenToUse: Use task flows when designing or reviewing a specific interaction such as registration, booking, purchasing, submitting information or completing a workflow.
steps: Establish the starting and completion conditions.
List the actions currently or potentially required.
Add decisions, alternative paths and system responses.
Compare the flow against research and technical constraints.
Prototype and test important flows with users.
lookOutFor: Do not design only the ideal path.
Include errors, interruptions, reversals and recovery where relevant.
A logically efficient flow may still be confusing when represented through an interface, so flow diagrams do not replace usability testing.

resources.citation: Hackos, J. T. & Redish, J. C. (1998). *User and Task Analysis for Interface Design*. Wiley.
